title: The heavyweight championship line (The Ring), 1950 onward
hook: Who has held boxing's heavyweight crown the longest?
caveat: Uses The Ring magazine heavyweight championship as the lineal proxy. Wikipedia lists no reign table for the 'lineal' title, whose succession is disputed (the Lineal championship article: 'the lineal championship may be subject to dispute'). The Ring stopped awarding the belt from 1989 to 2001, so that stretch is a vacancy here even though fan lineages continue through it.

source.name: Wikipedia: List of The Ring world champions (Heavyweight table), via MediaWiki API
source.terms: Wikipedia text is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 (attribution + share-alike); reuse of this derived data must credit Wikipedia contributors and carry the same licence.
source.notes: Reigns overlapping 1950-2025. Dates as the table gives them; month-only dates are set to the 1st with fromPrecision 'month'. A reign with no note in the table is taken to begin by beating the previous champion when the previous reign ended that same day. 'to: null' means current at revid 1374612889; series counts its days to 2025-12-31. Context page: Lineal championship (revid 1378319583). Cross-check: 19/21 reign start dates also appear verbatim in 'List of world heavyweight boxing champions' (revid 1374895974); not found there: #14 Floyd Patterson 1960-06-29, #25 Lennox Lewis 2001-12-02 (left as The Ring list gives them).

vacancies.reason: Ali was stripped of the title due to his refusal to be drafted to army service. Frazier was awarded the title in May.
New ownership discontinued the championship policy during Tyson's reign.
Lewis retired as champion and chose not to accept a rematch with Vitali Klitschko before a WBC-mandated 1 March deadline to accept the bout.
Vitali Klitschko retired after withdrawing from a bout against Hasim Rahman due to injuries.
Fury was stripped of the title for failing to declare an opponent by 31 January 2018, the deadline set by The Ring.
